implementation_notes: Vapor's Authentication module realizes the pattern: the user type conforms to Authenticatable, an Authenticator (basic, bearer, credentials, session, or a custom RequestAuthenticator) verifies the credential and logs the user in, and handlers read the descriptor with try req.auth.require(User.self) or the optional req.auth.get(User.self). Session-backed authentication stores only the identifier (SessionAuthenticatable) or a cached hash (CacheAuthenticatable) and reloads the user, which is the reload policy this pattern wants; the classic structure is replaced by the middleware group plus the Request.Authentication container. Keep the descriptor a small immutable struct and keep credentials out of it.
pitfalls: req.auth.require throws into the route's error handling; swallowing it or defaulting to an anonymous user turns a missing identity into an authorized request - keep guardMiddleware or require.

SessionAuthenticatable reloads by id per request, so a deleted or deactivated user still resolves unless the reload returns nil; CacheAuthenticatable caches the descriptor and needs explicit invalidation on revocation.
Fluent models are classes: sharing a model instance across requests lets one request's mutations change another's view of the identity - copy to a value-type descriptor at the boundary.
